# CLIP: four applications in a few lines

We will use 17 images and 17 captions to try four things: find a caption for an image, search with words, find similar images, and describe a change between two pictures. We use the same frozen CLIP model throughout.

In Colab, select **Runtime → Change runtime type → T4 GPU**, then **Run all**. CPU also works, but encoding is slower. The first run downloads OpenAI's ViT-B/32 weights (about 350 MB) and the small gallery. No API key or training is needed.

The saved outputs come from running the original OpenAI model on CPU. GPU rounding may differ slightly, as may the lecture's quantized browser scores. Once the gallery is encoded, change a query and rerun that cell.

[Lecture](https://author.github.io/attention/clip/) · [Image credits](https://author.github.io/attention/clip/lab/CREDITS.md) · [OpenAI CLIP](https://github.com/openai/CLIP)

# Colab already provides PyTorch, Pillow and Matplotlib.
%matplotlib inline
%config InlineBackend.figure_format = 'retina'

import sys, subprocess
if "google.colab" in sys.modules:
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-q",
        "git+https://github.com/openai/CLIP.git@d05afc436d78f1c48dc0dbf8e5980a9d471f35f6"])

cells.md:
## 1. Load the small database
Each record contains an image, its display name and a caption that we supplied. The gallery mixes the lecture's photographs with labelled generated examples. We number records from 0 to match Python's indexing. Two different captions can both fit an image; matching row and column numbers does not make a pair the only valid answer.

cells.code:
import json, math, textwrap, zipfile from pathlib import Path from urllib.request import urlretrieve import torch, clip import torch.nn.functional as F import matplotlib.pyplot as plt from PIL import Image from IPython.display import display, Markdown from html import escape plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 11, "axes.titlesize": 12, "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False, "figure.facecolor": "white", "axes.facecolor": "white"}) # Formatting only: the model calculations are in the cells below. def show_table(columns, rows): clean = lambda value: escape(str(value)).replace("|", "|").replace("\n", "
") lines = [" | ".join(columns), " | ".join(["---"] * len(columns))] lines += [" | ".join(clean(value) for value in row) for row in rows] display(Markdown("\n".join(lines))) a = Path("clip-mini-gallery.zip") if not a.exists(): urlretrieve("https://author.github.io/attention/clip/lab/clip-mini-gallery.zip", a) with zipfile.ZipFile(a) as z: z.extractall(".") root = Path("clip-mini-gallery") records = json.loads((root / "manifest.json").read_text()) images = [Image.open(root / r["file"]).convert("RGB") for r in records] captions = [r["caption"] for r in records] ids = {r["id"]: i for i, r in enumerate(records)} display(Markdown(f"Loaded **{len(images)} images** and **{len(captions)} supplied captions**. Here are five records:")) show_table(["Image / caption", "Image ID", "Caption sent to CLIP"], [[f"I{i} / T{i}", records[i]["id"], captions[i]] for i in [0, 1, 3, 7, 8]])

# A display helper only; the CLIP calculations stay in the cells below.
def show_images(indices, scores=None):
    indices = [int(i) for i in indices]
    cols = min(4, len(indices))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(math.ceil(len(indices)/cols), cols,
                             figsize=(3.3*cols, 4.2*math.ceil(len(indices)/cols)), squeeze=False,
                             layout="constrained")
    for ax in axes.flat:
        ax.axis("off")
    for ax, i in zip(axes.flat, indices):
        ax.imshow(images[i])
        ax.set_box_aspect(1)
        ax.set_title(textwrap.fill(f"I{i}: {records[i]['title']}", 29),
                     fontsize=11, fontweight="bold", color="#24334B", pad=10)
        label = textwrap.fill(f"T{i}: {captions[i]}", 34)
        if scores is not None:
            label += f"\nCosine: {float(scores[i]):+.3f}"
        ax.text(0.5, -0.04, label, transform=ax.transAxes,
                ha="center", va="top", fontsize=10, color="#394B61", linespacing=1.4)
    plt.show()

show_images(range(len(images)))

cells.md:
## 2. What goes into each encoder?
`preprocess` resizes/crops and normalizes RGB pixels. `tokenize` turns our captions into token IDs, with start/end tokens and padding to 77 positions. Filenames and gallery titles are never model inputs.

cells.code:
device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
model, preprocess = clip.load("ViT-B/32", device=device)
model.eval()
x = torch.stack([preprocess(im) for im in images]).to(device)
tokens = clip.tokenize(captions).to(device)
print(f"Model: ViT-B/32    Device: {device}")
show_table(["Input", "Shape", "What each dimension means"], [
    ["x (images)", tuple(x.shape), "images, RGB channels, height, width"],
    ["tokens (text)", tuple(tokens.shape), "captions, token positions"]])
show_table(["Caption", "First 12 token IDs"],
           [[captions[i], tokens[i, :12].tolist()] for i in [0, 1, 3]])

cells.md:
## 3. Encode once, then normalize
`encode_image` and `encode_text` include their learned projections. Each output has 512 coordinates. Divide **each row** by its own length so a dot product becomes a cosine. The encoders' weights stay fixed throughout this lab.

cells.code:
with torch.inference_mode():
    z_image = model.encode_image(x).float()
    z_text = model.encode_text(tokens).float()
U = F.normalize(z_image, dim=-1)  # one unit image vector per row
V = F.normalize(z_text, dim=-1)   # one unit text vector per row
show_table(["Vector array", "Shape", "First row: first 6 of 512 coordinates"],
           [[name, tuple(value.shape), ", ".join(f"{v:+.3f}" for v in value[0, :6].tolist())]
            for name, value in [("Raw images z_image", z_image), ("Raw text z_text", z_text),
                                ("Unit images U", U), ("Unit text V", V)]])
show_table(["Image row", "Raw length", "Length after normalization"],
           [[f"I{i}", f"{z_image[i].norm():.3f}", f"{U[i].norm():.6f}"] for i in range(3)])

cells.md:
## 4. One matrix contains every image-caption comparison
`U @ V.T` has **image rows** and **caption columns**. Entry `[i, j]` compares image `Ii` with caption `Tj`. These are raw cosines, not probabilities. We do not need temperature or softmax just to rank candidates.

cells.code:
C = U @ V.T
print("[17, 512] @ [512, 17] →", tuple(C.shape))
show_table(["Calculation", "Cosine"], [["C[0, 0]", f"{C[0, 0]:.6f}"],
           ["dot(U[0], V[0])", f"{torch.dot(U[0], V[0]):.6f}"]])
plt.figure(figsize=(7, 6))
plt.imshow(C.cpu(), cmap="viridis")
plt.xticks(range(17), [f"T{i}" for i in range(17)], rotation=90)
plt.yticks(range(17), [f"I{i}" for i in range(17)])
plt.title("Every image against every supplied caption", pad=14)
plt.xlabel("Supplied caption columns"); plt.ylabel("Image rows")
plt.colorbar(label="Cosine similarity"); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

cells.md:
## 5. Given an image, find its closest captions
Pick one **row** of `C`. CLIP ranks our captions; it does not write a new caption. Try `rocket`, `red-mug`, or `retriever-sketch`.

cells.code:
image_id = "newfoundland"  # change this
q = ids[image_id]
show_images([q])
scores = C[q]  # shape [17]: this image against every caption
print("Caption scores:", tuple(scores.shape))
show_table(["Rank", "Caption", "Supplied text", "Cosine"],
           [[rank, f"T{j}", captions[j], f"{scores[j]:+.3f}"]
            for rank, j in enumerate(scores.argsort(descending=True)[:5].tolist(), 1)])

cells.md:
## 6. Given words, find images
We can supply a new query that was never in the original caption list. Encode it with the same text encoder and compare it with every cached image vector. Try `something to drink`, `a pet`, or `solar panels`.

cells.code:
query = "something to drink"  # change this
with torch.inference_mode():
    z_query = model.encode_text(clip.tokenize([query]).to(device)).float()
v_query = F.normalize(z_query, dim=-1)
scores = (U @ v_query.T).squeeze(1)
print("[17, 512] @", tuple(v_query.T.shape), "→ 17 image scores")
print("Query:", query)
show_images(scores.argsort(descending=True)[:4].tolist(), scores)

out.text:
[17, 512] @ (512, 1) → 17 image scores
Query: something to drink

cells.md:
## 7. Given an image, find similar images
This uses only image vectors. Exclude the query itself: its cosine with itself is approximately 1. Try the Persian cat, the red mug, or the generated dog photograph.

cells.code:
image_id = "Persian"  # try "red-mug" or "retriever-photo"
q = ids[image_id]
show_images([q])
scores = U @ U[q]  # [17, 512] @ [512] → [17]
scores[q] = -torch.inf  # do not retrieve the query itself
show_images(scores.argsort(descending=True)[:4].tolist(), scores)

cells.md:
## 8. Which words line up with a change?
Show both images first. Subtract **after − before**, using their unit image vectors, and normalize the difference again. Compare that direction with supplied candidate words.

The edited pictures already exist: CLIP neither creates the edit nor generates its explanation. Other changes in the pair can influence the ranking.

cells.code:
before_id, after_id = "portrait", "portrait-hat"
words = ["hat", "boat", "cup", "cat"]
before, after = ids[before_id], ids[after_id]
show_images([before, after])
delta = U[after] - U[before]
length = delta.norm()
if length < 1e-6:
    raise ValueError("The two images have no stable change direction.")
d = delta / length
with torch.inference_mode():
    W = F.normalize(model.encode_text(clip.tokenize(words).to(device)).float(), dim=-1)
change_scores = W @ d
show_table(["Quantity", "Shape", "Length"], [
    ["after - before", tuple(delta.shape), f"{length:.6f}"],
    ["Unit change direction d", tuple(d.shape), f"{d.norm():.6f}"]])
print(f"[{len(words)}, 512] @ [512] → {tuple(change_scores.shape)}")
show_table(["Candidate word", "Cosine with the change"],
           [[words[j], f"{change_scores[j]:+.4f}"] for j in change_scores.argsort(descending=True).tolist()])

cells.md:
### Two quick checks, then try another pair
Reversing the edit negates the scores. Changing the candidate words changes what the ranking can tell us.

- Red to blue: `red-mug`, `blue-mug`; words `['blue', 'red', 'cup', 'hat']`.
- Photo to sketch: `retriever-photo`, `retriever-sketch`; words `['pencil sketch', 'photograph', 'dog', 'cat']`.
- Reverse either pair. Which scores switch sign?
- Give the dog image a caption menu with no dogs. Why does the top answer still not prove it is correct?

cells.code:
reverse_scores = W @ (-d)
show_table(["Candidate", "Forward: after - before", "Reverse: before - after"],
           [[word, f"{forward:+.4f}", f"{reverse:+.4f}"]
            for word, forward, reverse in zip(words, change_scores.tolist(), reverse_scores.tolist())])
print("Reversal check:", torch.allclose(reverse_scores, -change_scores, atol=1e-6))
print("All gallery vectors have unit length:",
      torch.allclose(U.norm(dim=1), torch.ones(len(images), device=device), atol=1e-5))

out.text:
Reversal check: True
All gallery vectors have unit length: True

cells.md:
## What stayed the same?
All four applications reused the same frozen encoders and cached gallery vectors. We changed only the query and the dot product. Similarity is a ranking signal within these choices, not a guarantee about what an image contains.

To run locally: install `torch torchvision matplotlib Pillow jupyterlab` and the pinned OpenAI CLIP package from the setup cell, then run this notebook with a Python 3 kernel. The saved reference run used Python 3.12 and PyTorch 2.13 on CPU.
